description: A bunch of people with varying levels of questionable technical knowledge, absolutely no idea what we're doing, and a shared belief that space is really, really cool and so is coding.
summary:
Orb.Ignite is an AI powered all-round dashboard built for researchers, mission planners, or students learning about life in space.
Due to a history of unfortunate accidents, behaviour of fire in space has come to light and is being researched. Fires in microgravity behave differently to their earth counter-parts, even forming spherical, soot-free "cool flames" which are invisible in some cases posing severe risks to crewed spacecrafts or equipment.
Using the avaiable data from various experiment's from NASA's PSI repository, combined with research material from NTRS and independent platforms, four main features have been implemented.A Mission & Experiment Catalog (covering FLEX, Saffire, SoFIE, ACME, BASS, SAME, SPICE, and DAFT), a Real-Time 3D Flame Lab visualizing gravity, oxygen, and airflow effects on flame morphology, an Fire Predictor forecasting burn duration, burning rate, fire regime, and crew/vehicle hazard and an AI Research Assistant for Q&A.
details:
THE WHAT:

Orb.Ignite transforms years of fragmented microgravity combustion flight data and experimental results into a dynamic dashboard, combining NASA datasets, technical research, machine learning, analytical physics, and interactive visualisations.

CONSISTS OF:

Four main features:

  1. Mission Catalog & Knowledge Base: Indexes NASA spaceflight and ground-based combustion experiments, including FLEX / FLEX-2, Saffire, SoFIE, ACME, BASS, SAME, SPICE, SLICE, DAFT, and others, alongside relevant NTRS technical reports and fire-safety protocols.
  2. Real-Time 3D Flame Lab: Uses interactive 3D volumetric rendering to visualise how gravity, oxygen concentration, and ventilation airflow influence flame geometry, thermal gradients, and flame morphology.
  3. Fire Hazard Predictor: Predicts flame persistence, burn duration, burning rate, extinction diameter, fire regime, and quantitative crew and vehicle hazard metrics with the help of XGBoost. Models are retrained whenever an admin makes changes to the training data. Analytical Grashof/Rayleigh-based physics models complement ML predictions where experimental flight data is limited, with explicit Data-backed and Theory-based confidence tiers.
  4. AI Research Assistant: Uses the Gemini API to answer technical questions grounded in indexed NASA NTRS reports, backed by a zero-cloud fallback architecture using local physics equations, JSON catalogs, and keyword search.

Authentication is handled by Supabase.

Data has undergone editing and preprocessing before model training and testing. Super Intelligence has also been used to identify usable data, train the models, and extract the respective predictions.

DESIGN QUIRKS:

A very indirect reference to the idea of flying too close to flames has been included. Playlists of NASA tunes and wake-up music were originally planned, but due to difficulties with Spotify integration, only 10 tracks were selected, alongside 3 fallback lo-fi tracks. The background features auroras corresponding to the selected preset, and the theme can be changed by pulling the moon or the sun. Stars have also been added to the sidebar to complement the space theme, and appropriate colours have been chosen to denote warnings and hazards. At the end, the project has also been signed by the team :).

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED:

  • Language & Framework: Python, Streamlit, HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript
  • Machine Learning & Data: XGBoost, scikit-learn, Joblib, Pandas, NumPy
  • Visualisation & UI: Plotly (3D volumetric rendering), Inter, Public Sans, DM Mono, Ms Madi
  • Cloud, Deployment & AI Services: Google Cloud Run, Google Cloud Build, Artifact Registry, Docker, Google Gemini , Supabase
  • Additional Integrations: Spotify API (spotipy), SMTP (smtplib, email)

THE INTENDED IMPACT:

Makes fragmented microgravity combustion research easier to access, explore, and analyse, supporting a better understanding of spacecraft fire behaviour and crew safety during future space missions.

Orb.Ignite - Orbiting the Flames of Flight.

After all, not all flames are meant to be flown too close to.
